newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-PARMA ENTER CHAMPIONS' LEAGUE WITH JUVENTUS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PARMA ENTER CHAMPIONS' LEAGUE WITH JUVENTUS.

text.p: Parma, who have never won the Italian title, secured a place in the Champions' League after beating relegated Verona 2-1 on Sunday to finish the serie A season as runners-up to Juventus.
Juventus clinched the title nine days ago and celebrated at home in Turin after drawing 2-2 with Lazio, who came back from 2-0 down on a wet day at the Delle Alpi stadium.

Argentine striker Hernan Crespo scored the 64th minute winner for Parma after Verona had taken the lead at home through Pierluigi Orlandini in the sixth minute. Italy international Enrico Chiesa levelled the score after 17 minutes.
Internazionale drew 2-2 with Bologna to finish the season third and four points behind Parma.
Juventus ended with 65 points to Parma's 63.
Udinese made sure of a UEFA Cup place for the first time in their history by beating 10-man Roma 3-0 to finish fifth after Lazio. It was their best placing since 1957.
Sampdoria took the final UEFA slot.
Sampdoria's 1-1 draw with Fiorentina marked the farewell of striker Roberto Mancini after 15 seasons. He is expected to join coach Sven-Goran Eriksson at Lazio next season.
Roma had goalkeeper Gianluca Berti sent off in the 27th minute for a professional foul.
Vicenza secured the Cup Winners' Cup berth on Thursday night when they beat Napoli in the Italian Cup final that was cast as a battle between north and south.

Napoli took a measure of revenge at home on Sunday by beating Vicenza 1-0, with Brazilian Beto -- who was on the bench for the Cup final second leg -- scoring the fourth minute goal before the club's smallest crowd of the season.
At the bottom, Piacenza pulled off a remarkable escape act by beating Perugia 2-1, condemning them to serie B after fellow strugglers Cagliari also won.
Perugia fans set fire to banners and debris at Piacenza's Galleana stadium after the defeat, sending thick smoke over the pitch. The flames were swiftly put out.
Under complicated rules based on direct confrontations, Cagliari and Piacenza must now play again at a neutral venue, probably on June 15, to decide which of the two survives.

The result meant Piacenza midfielder Eusebio Di Francesco, called up for Italy on Friday, will probably be unavailable for the four-nation Tournoi de France starting next week as his club will need him for the relegation playoff.

Piacenza striker Pasquale Luiso scored in the 29th minute with a diving header and defender Settimio Lucci made it 2-0 with a 48th minute penalty. Perugia finally found the net in the 90th minute through Giacomo Dicara.
Roberto Muzzi scored in the 10th minute as Cagliari beat 10-man Milan 1-0 at San Siro to finish level on points with Piacenza and Perugia.
Cagliari could have been 2-0 up by halftime but Milan's Sebastiano Rossi saved a 42nd minute penalty.

Milan, with 37-year-old defender Mauro Tassotti playing his last match for the club after 17 seasons, lost Montenegrin striker Dejan Savicevic in the 19th minute after he insulted a linesman while preparing for a corner.
The match may also have been the last at Milan for 36-year-old defender Franco Baresi.
Atalanta's Filippo Inzaghi scored twice in a 3-0 demolition of Reggiana to finish the season as top serie A scorer with 24 goals, ahead of Sampdoria's Vincenzo Montella on 22.
